messages:
incident-bot: ALERT — spike detected: api-gateway edge returning 502/504s. 5m error rate 8.7% (baseline <0.5%). Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/edge/edge-errors?orgId=1 :rotating_light:

maria: i'm paged, jumping in. linking eng-runtime and platform. starting triage now.

kyla: seeing corresponding increase in downstream timeouts to upstream pool 'model-backend' (p50->p95 increased). traces show many upstream timeouts (504) and some envoy masked 502.

maria: rolling up current hypothesis: sudden downstream backlog + a recent config change to the edge rate-limiter around 02:58Z. need to check recent deploys. @jess can you check config deploys?

jess: checking deploys... last config push to edge-proxy was 02:56Z by infra-ci (sha: a1b2c3). it's a minor throttle tweak to global_conn_limit. no other infra deploys in the window.

tony: i'll tail the edge pods and health checks. running:
```
kubectl -n infra get pods -l app=edge-proxy -o wide
kubectl -n infra logs -l app=edge-proxy --tail=200
```

maria: logs show repeated errors from envoy: "upstream response timeout" and occasional "connection reset by peer". sample:
```
[2024-06-12T02:59:12Z] proxy error: upstream timed out (110) while reading response header from upstream "10.12.8.21:8080"
[2024-06-12T03:00:05Z] 502 POST /v1/generate  0.62s
```

kyla: also seeing a sharp drop in successful handshakes to model-backend (TLS handshake failures spiking). possible network flakiness or overloaded backend.

tony: quick mitigation options:
- increase edge-proxy replicas to absorb burst
- open an emergency bypass route for /v1/generate to route to a warm fallback model cluster
- roll back the global_conn_limit tweak
Which should we try first? :thinking_face:

maria: start with scale + fallback. rollbacks take a few minutes to propagate and we need immediate capacity. jess can rollback if needed. tony scale now. set replicas + autoscaler throttle.

tony: scaling now:
```
kubectl -n infra scale deploy edge-proxy --replicas=12
kubectl -n infra get hpa edge-proxy -o yaml
```

ops-bot (automated): scaling initiated for deploy/edge-proxy -> 12 replicas. PodReady counts increasing.

sam: product note — we'll see 502s on user-facing /v1/generate and some slow responses on chat endpoints. I've flagged CS with template: "We're investigating increased errors for API requests; engineers are mitigating."

kyla: while scaling, i'm enabling a quick route to fallback-models:
```
# temporary routing change
route /v1/generate -> svc:fallback-models:8080 priority=lower
```

jess: started rollback of config tweak (triggered at 03:06Z). rolling back to sha: z9y8x7. watch logs for success.

maria: results so far: after scaling + fallback the error rate dropped from 8.7% -> 1.5% in the last 2 minutes. p95 latency still a bit elevated. keep monitoring.

tony: observed a noisy node in k8s cluster: node-az3 had repeated pod restarts for model-backend (OOMKill + TCP resets). cordoning node-az3 and draining affected pods. commands:
```
kubectl cordon node-az3
kubectl drain node-az3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

kyla: after cordon+drain, handshake failures dropped by 90%. looks like a faulty network interface on node-az3.

maria: i'm handing over to tony for next steps — i've got another page. handoff at 03:12Z. tony you're primary. I'll remain on slack but handing paging. :white_check_mark:

tony: acknowledged. I'll keep running mitigation and own the incident. next actions:
- keep fallback-route active for 30m
- validate rollback completed and monitor for config drift
- open incident ticket with timeline and affected customers
- plan postmortem owner: jess + kyla for infra/network, tony for runtime

sam: estimated customer impact: ~2.1% of total requests returned 5xx during 02:58Z-03:12Z window. two customers reported elevated errors; CS already notified.

jess: rollback completed at 03:09Z, confirmed via deploy logs. no further config pushes since.

tony: closing triage loop for now — error rate stabilized ~0.4%. keeping the fallback route for 20 more minutes and will remove once stable. creating incident ticket: https://incidents.redwood.local/INC-2024-0456 (owner: tony).

maria: thanks team — good quick work. tony please update this thread with final timeline and RCA owner.

tony: will do. current last_check 03:22Z shows steady metrics. next: full RCA and remediation plan (replace faulty node, add better node health checks, add circuit breaker for model-backend).

incident-bot: Incident INC-2024-0456 created and assigned to tony. Severity: P2.

tony: assigning postmortem to jess (infra) + kyla (observability). will send follow-up. :memo:
